title: Sherfey v. James River Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC ruled the complaint judicially out of order with incurable defects. Several asserted errors had not first been adjudicated by James River Presbytery, and the General Assembly filing also missed BCO 43-3’s thirty-day deadline. The SJC did not reach the merits or order a remand.
first_summary: Sherfey challenged James River Presbytery’s denial of his complaint and alleged errors in its commission’s proceedings. The SJC ruled his complaint judicially out of order with incurable defects because several grounds had not first been adjudicated by Presbytery and his General Assembly filing was late. Although a concurrence proposed returning the complaint to Presbytery, the adopted decision neither reached the merits nor specified further proceedings.
summary: Sherfey challenged James River Presbytery’s denial of his complaint and alleged errors in its commission’s proceedings. The SJC ruled the complaint judicially out of order with incurable defects: several grounds had not first been adjudicated by Presbytery as BCO 43-2 required, and the General Assembly filing missed BCO 43-3’s thirty-day deadline. Incorrect advice from Presbytery’s clerk did not excuse compliance. The adopted decision neither reached the merits nor ordered a remand; only a concurrence proposed returning the matter to Presbytery.

sources.supports: Case identity, adopted disposition and reasons, filing defect, vote, and the separate concurrence.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Title and SJC adoption appear at printed pp. 562–563, lines 11 and 25–31.
evidence_notes.dispute: The complaint combined alleged errors concerning the Session matter with new objections to Presbytery’s commission and judgment; printed p. 562, line 15. The concurrence lists the asserted grounds at printed pp. 563–564, lines 39–47.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The adopted decision declares incurable judicial out-of-order defects because several grounds were unadjudicated under BCO 43-2; it also notes the missed BCO 43-3 deadline and rejects reliance on incorrect clerk advice. Printed pp. 562–563, lines 13–23.
evidence_notes.qualifications: The adopted decision merely reminds presbyteries to consider BCO Appendix H. It orders no remand; the proposed return to Presbytery appears only in the concurrence. Printed pp. 563, 565, lines 23–25 and 80–82.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No decision is incorporated by reference.

source_limits: The source supplies the adopted ruling and a concurrence but not the underlying record. The concurrence’s procedural criticism and proposed next step are not holdings.

verification_notes: Rechecked the operative ruling at lines 13–25 against the concurrence at lines 39–82. The final summary clarifies that the adopted SJC decision—notwithstanding the concurrence—ordered no remand and that incorrect clerk advice did not excuse the filing deadline.
